newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Britain urges haste from Vietnam on boatpeople.
newsitem.headline: Britain urges haste from Vietnam on boatpeople.

text.p: British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said on Saturday that time was running short for a solution to Hong Kong's boatpeople problem, and he urged Vietnam to do more to overcome a repatriation blockage.

Rifkind told a news conference in the Vietnamese capital that with just months to go before Hong Kong returns to Chinese rule, there was no time for further delays in plans to empty the colony's boatpeople camps of their remaining 12,000 inmates.

He said there were still a number of boatpeople in Hong Kong whose names had not been cleared by Hanoi for repatriation, and that a problem had arisen over Vietnam's refusal to recognise some as its own nationals.

"All the people we are referring to are people who came from Vietnam to Hong Kong... It is right, therefore, that they should return to Vietnam and it is the objective to ensure that happens by June 30th."
Rifkind met Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam on Friday to discuss the issue and told foreign journalists afterwards that Cam had recognised the need to expedite the return process.
He said on Saturday he looked forward to seeing Vietnam's proposals now to resolve the outstanding blockages, and hoped these would appear soon.
Hong Kong is home to the largest remaining boatpeople population in East Asia, the last of a vast wave who fled their country in rickety boats after the Vietnam War ended in 1975.
In October, some 1,700 Vietnamese were repatriated from the British colony, representing the highest monthly total in years.

But concerned groups and others have warned that the final phase of the 20-year boatpeople saga is likely to face problems with resistance from people who have held out against deportation, in some cases for many years.

Rifkind was due to leave Hanoi later on Saturday. During his visit he also discussed growing trade and commercial links between Britain and Vietnam, but said the two sides had yet to reach agreement on investment issues.
The United Kingdom currently is 13th among foreign investors in Vietnam with some $485 million pledged towards 19 projects.
